_doc: Every source the Western module cites. 'school' keeps traditions apart: hellenistic (Greek-language astrology of the Roman era), traditional (medieval/Renaissance, here Lilly), modern (19th-20th century psychological / theosophical astrology), astronomy (computation), convention (a choice Thiên Bàn makes where no authority settles it). A rule may cite only sources of its own school, plus astronomy.

PTOL_TETRA.author: Claudius Ptolemy
PTOL_TETRA.title: Tetrabiblos
PTOL_TETRA.edition: tr. F. E. Robbins, Loeb Classical Library 435 (1940)
PTOL_TETRA.rights: public domain (US copyright not renewed, per LacusCurtius)
PTOL_TETRA.note: Ptolemy is Hellenistic in date but systematises in his own way (no lot reversal by night, terms of his own, no decans); where he and Valens differ both are kept.

LILLY_CA.author: William Lilly
LILLY_CA.title: Christian Astrology
LILLY_CA.note: Lilly's dignity table (p.104) follows 'Ptolomy' for triplicities (day/night only) and terms. Page images: Wellcome Collection copy b30338724 (PDF page = printed page + 34).

VALENS_ANTH.author: Vettius Valens
VALENS_ANTH.title: Anthologies
VALENS_ANTH.edition: tr. Mark T. Riley (2010, distributed free by the translator)
VALENS_ANTH.rights: translation in copyright, used for short citations and paraphrase only

LEO.author: Alan Leo
LEO.title: The Progressed Horoscope (1906); How to Judge a Nativity (1928 printing); The Art of Synthesis (1926 printing); Astrology for All (1910)

JPL_DE440.author: R. S. Park, W. M. Folkner, J. G. Williams, D. H. Boggs
JPL_DE440.title: The JPL Planetary and Lunar Ephemerides DE440 and DE441

JPL_HORIZONS.title: JPL Horizons system
JPL_HORIZONS.note: Chiron state vectors (solution JPL#171) and spot checks of apparent positions.

SKYFIELD.author: Brandon Rhodes
SKYFIELD.title: Skyfield
SKYFIELD.note: apparent positions (light time, aberration, deflection), IAU 2000A nutation, true ecliptic and equinox of date

SWE_DOC.author: Astrodienst (D. Koch, A. Treindl)
SWE_DOC.title: Swiss Ephemeris documentation
SWE_DOC.note: definitions of the house systems and of the true (osculating) node; Swiss Ephemeris itself is used only as a test reference (AGPL).

GEONAMES.title: GeoNames gazetteer
GEONAMES.rights: CC BY 4.0 (attribution shown on the page)

TZDB.title: IANA time zone database
TZDB.note: historical offsets and DST; Asia/Hanoi from the backzone file

CONV_ORBS.title: Thiên Bàn orb table
CONV_ORBS.note: No book fixes orbs for the modern school; Thiên Bàn's numbers are a stated convention and can be changed.

CONV_MINOR.title: Minor aspects
CONV_MINOR.note: 30, 45, 135, 150, 72, 144 degrees: in use since Kepler (Harmonices Mundi, 1619) and in modern practice; not part of the Hellenistic or Lilly's doctrine.

CONV_PATTERNS.title: Aspect configurations
CONV_PATTERNS.note: grand trine, T-square, grand cross, yod, kite, mystic rectangle, stellium: 20th-century modern vocabulary; geometric definitions only.

CONV_MODERN_RULERS.title: Modern co-rulers
CONV_MODERN_RULERS.note: Uranus-Aquarius, Neptune-Pisces, Pluto-Scorpio: 20th-century convention after the outer planets' discovery; shown only when the modern ruler option is chosen.
